    Effect sizes of invasion impact

    Source: R/inv-impact.R
    inv_impact_metrics.Rd

    Compares a response (native richness, cover, biomass, a soil property) between invaded and reference (uninvaded) plots and returns the log response ratio (Hedges et al. 1999), Hedges' bias-corrected standardised mean difference g, and the percentage change, with confidence intervals.

    Usage

    inv_impact_metrics(
  .data,
  response,
  status,
  invaded = "invaded",
  .by = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per plot or sample.

    response

    <tidy-select> Numeric response column.

    status

    <tidy-select> Column with the invasion status of each row. It must have exactly two values.

    invaded

    Value of status that marks invaded rows. The other value is the reference.

    .by

    <tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, for example site or response variable.

    conf_level

    Confidence level.

    Value

    A tibble with one row per group: sample sizes, means and standard deviations of both groups, lnrr with lnrr_var, lnrr_low and lnrr_high, hedges_g with hedges_g_var, g_low and g_high, and pct_change (100 * (exp(lnrr) - 1)). The log response ratio is NA when either mean is not positive.

    References

    Hedges, L. V., Gurevitch, J. and Curtis, P. S. (1999). The meta-analysis of response ratios in experimental ecology. Ecology, 80, 1150-1156.

    Examples

    inv_impact_metrics(inv_plots, response = native_richness, status = status,
  .by = site)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 16
#>   site   n_invaded n_reference mean_invaded mean_reference sd_invaded
#>   <chr>      <int>       <int>        <dbl>          <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 site_1         8           8         13             19.8       4.07
#> 2 site_2         8           8         23.1           31.9       2.47
#> 3 site_3         8           8          9             17         2.39
#> 4 site_4         8           8         13.8           15.1       4.23
#> 5 site_5         8           8         16.6           17         4.14
#> 6 site_6         8           8         13.5           24.9       4.17
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: sd_reference <dbl>, lnrr <dbl>, lnrr_var <dbl>,
#> #   lnrr_low <dbl>, lnrr_high <dbl>, hedges_g <dbl>, hedges_g_var <dbl>,
#> #   g_low <dbl>, g_high <dbl>, pct_change <dbl>
